# The following regex pattern matches an ISO calendar date: YYYY-MM-DD
# where year is from 1900 to 2099, month and day are from 01 to 31 (per year).
# It rejects:
#   - Non-iso formats (e.g., "1969/03/15")

#   - Year out of bounds (e.g., "1964-07-32" has invalid numbers)
#   - Leap month on days > 29 (e.g., "1807-03-15", "1607-02-28", etc.)
#   - Any non-digits/non-hyphens before or after (e.g., "1964-07-32 extra")

pattern = r"^(\d{4})-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}$"
regex = re.compile(pattern)

# This regex does not check per-month validity for valid inputs like "2023-01-31" or "2024-13-03".
# It only ensures the format matches YYYY-MM-DD with ranges as required.

```regex
^SO-[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{6}[-R][1-9]$
```

**Explanation of the pattern:**  
`^SO-` : Anchors the start with "SO-"  
`[A-Z]{2}` : Exactly 2 uppercase ASCII letters (e.g., QK, BC)  
`-[0-9]{6}` : A hyphen followed by exactly 7 digits (the first part of the ID)  
`[-R]` : Optionally a hyphen followed by "R" or nothing at all (for the revision suffix)  
`[1-9]$` : Finally, one digit from 1 to 9 at the end of the string (the revision digit)

This fully captures all valid cases while rejecting strings with mismatched lengths, missing suffixes, extra characters outside the defined format.
